# Three-fiber boundary crossflow and one conditional midpoint law

This note retains the actual physical boundary transport behind the planar
aggregate in `candidate 915dc3adcfe3fcf0`.
It identifies the nonaffine base-weight deficit exactly, localizes it to
actual midpoint contact normals, and constructs one midpoint law giving
literal closed-cap credit for every ambient cap simultaneously. A given
conditional law need not have any boundary density, even when both
endpoint target marginals have bounded constant densities. In the plane
one can nevertheless select a different entire martingale whose midpoint
law is dominated by middle boundary length. It does not assert a mixed
depth bound or a critical-body classification.

## 1. Actual measures, normalization, and hypotheses

Let d>=2 and let K_-, K_0, K_+ be positive compact convex bodies with

    (K_-+K_+)/2 subset K_0.                         (1)

They are the three sampled fibers at bases -1,0,1 of an actual convex
family. Write h_z for their support functions. On the compact normal
bundle record (n,z,X), with |n|=1 and X in K_z(n), let eta_z be ordinary
surface measure with its almost-everywhere unique outward normal, and
put eta=sum_z eta_z. Its normal marginal is S_z. Auxiliary measures below
can charge singular boundary points, so their normal coordinate must not
be discarded or replaced by a guessed unique normal.

Let theta be a probability law of ACTUAL ambient caps, with the chosen
consistent physical body selectors s_H in [0,1], including the supporting
allocations. Define

    W(n,z,X)=int s_H(n,z,X) dtheta(H),
    nu=(W/beta) eta,                 0<beta<1.       (2)

Assume an actual normal-preserving physical martingale from nu to eta:

    Pi(ds,dt)=nu(ds) P_s(dt),
    (n)_*P_s=delta_(n_s),
    int (z_t,X_t) P_s(dt)=(z_s,X_s).               (3)

Here Pi has second marginal eta. The kernel is a probability kernel
nu-almost everywhere. All spaces are compact Borel spaces, so ordinary
disintegration applies. Equation (3), rather than just a normal marginal
identity, is an explicit hypothesis. The ordinary full normal-convex
stress can supply it where its complete convex-order conclusion is
available. No independent source-group stress is assumed.

In particular nu and eta have the same mass and normal marginal. The
physical source and target are not interchanged in any formula below.

## 2. Exact nonaffine deficit and strict-surplus support

An endpoint source can target only its own base: a probability on
{-1,0,1} with mean +1 or -1 is concentrated at that endpoint. A middle
source s therefore has

    P_s(z_t=-1)=P_s(z_t=1)=q(s),   0<=q(s)<=1/2.    (4)

Let gamma_- and gamma_+ be the physical target measures of the two
crossflows from middle sources to their respective endpoints. They are
submeasures of eta_- and eta_+. Their normal marginals coincide:

    tau=(n)_*gamma_-=(n)_*gamma_+
       =(n)_*[q(s) nu_0(ds)].                       (5)

Endpoint-source rows can move tangentially on endpoint faces. Consequently
one must NOT assert gamma_z=eta_z-nu_z as physical measures. The following
identities are identities of NORMAL measures and do hold:

    (n)_*(W eta_-)=beta(S_- - tau),
    (n)_*(W eta_+)=beta(S_+ - tau),
    (n)_*(W eta_0)=beta(S_0 + 2tau).                (6)

They follow by splitting the target marginal according to its source
base; every row preserves n. Thus for the convex base weight |z| the
positive deficit is exactly

    D:=beta(S_-+S_+) - (n)_*[W(eta_-+eta_+)]
      =2 beta tau.                                 (7)

For a middle source with normal n, take n times its continuous barycenter
equation. Every target lies in the corresponding support face, so

    h_0(n)=(1-2q(s))h_0(n)+q(s)[h_-(n)+h_+(n)].

By (1), this proves

    q(s)[2h_0(n)-h_-(n)-h_+(n)]=0.                 (8)

Let Z={n: h_-(n)+h_+(n)=2h_0(n)}. Then

    tau is supported on Z,
    0<=tau<=1_Z(S_- wedge S_+),
    0<=D<=2 beta 1_Z(S_- wedge S_+).                (9)

The wedge is the greatest common submeasure. No density with respect to
spherical Lebesgue measure is assumed. Thus every strictly positive
midpoint support surplus forces zero crossflow and zero deficit at that
normal. The archived common-area/contact theorem additionally gives

    1_Z(S_- wedge S_+) <= 1_Z S_0,                  (10)

but (10) alone is not new: see
`candidate 0c3c4405d9ae2dd3` and
`candidate d332d092619053f4`.
The new information here is the exact actual-flow identification (7)
and the physical conditional law in the next section.

If the common endpoint area on Z is zero, tau=0. Then all three source
bases preserve their base and each individual fiber has the normal
marginal identity (n)_*(W eta_z)=beta S_z. In d=2 the audited planar
construction consequently gives an individual section body J_z with

    J_z+v_z subset (1-beta)K_z,
    -J_z+v'_z subset beta K_z.                     (11)

These are the section bodies for the SAME cap law and allocations.
They are not the original aggregate J, and no general Gamma payment is
claimed from (11). Condition (9), rather than a parity regrouping,
is what permits this local conclusion.

## 3. One conditional endpoint pairing and a physical middle martingale

For q(s)>0, disintegrate the endpoint branches into probability kernels
P_s^- and P_s^+. Choose their conditional independent product, or any one
measurable conditional coupling. Define a tuple measure of mass int q dnu_0:

    Xi(ds,dt_-,dt_+)
       =q(s) nu_0(ds) [P_s^- tensor P_s^+](dt_-,dt_+). (12)

The two target marginals are exactly gamma_- and gamma_+. Both targets
have the source normal. Push Xi by

    (n,-1,X_-; n,1,X_+) -> (n,0,(X_-+X_+)/2)

to a measure rho. Equation (8) and actual midpoint inclusion show that
rho is supported on the middle normal bundle and

    (n)_*rho=tau.                                  (13)

This conclusion includes nonsmooth middle boundary points; rho need not
be dominated by eta_0.

In each middle-source row keep its original base-zero target branch,
of mass 1-2q, and replace its two endpoint branches by twice the paired
midpoint branch. The result is a probability kernel with the same
continuous barycenter as that source. Only middle sources can feed a
base-zero target, so the retained base-zero target marginal is exactly
eta_0. Hence this construction is an actual same-normal martingale

    nu_0  ->  eta_0+2rho.                            (14)

In particular nu_0 is below eta_0+2rho in physical convex order, including
normal-localized convex tests. The two sides have equal mass; no missing
normalization factor is absorbed into rho.

For every closed ambient halfspace H={az+u.X>=c}, the SAME tuple law has
the pointwise inequality

    1_H(-1,X_-)+1_H(1,X_+)
       >= 1_H(0,(X_-+X_+)/2).

Therefore, simultaneously for every such H,

    gamma_-(H)+gamma_+(H) >= rho(H_0).              (15)

There is no separate coupling chosen for different caps. One may
integrate (15) against any cap law. This is literal closed-cap credit.
It must not be silently substituted for an inequality between arbitrary
supporting allocations s_H. At support coincidences, those allocations
are additional data rather than the closed indicator. If the relevant
allocated traces agree with the literal indicators on these measures,
the corresponding weighted version follows immediately. Otherwise a
common first-order selector implication would have to be proved.

Likewise (14) gives inequalities for convex tests, not for halfspace
indicators. Combining (14) and (15) does not by itself compare captured
nu_0 with captured endpoint flow.

## 4. Actual cap-law obstruction to automatic midpoint density

Take d=2, K_-=K_0=K_+=[-1,1]^2. This is the actual complete three-fiber
family of the product [-1,1] times [-1,1]^2. Put b=1/3. Use the eight
actual caps, each with probability 1/8,

    H_(v,a)={az+v.X>=-b},
    v in {e_1,-e_1,e_2,-e_2},  a in {-2,2}.        (16)

Every boundary trace used below is proper or full/empty up to finitely
many length-zero intersection points; no positive-length supporting
allocation is needed. At either endpoint base exactly half the caps
capture the whole square, so W_-=W_+=1/2. On any middle edge write

    X=n+t e,        -1<=t<=1,

where n is its outward coordinate normal and e a unit tangent. Then

    W_0(n+t e)=3/4  if |t|<1/3,
                 1/2  if |t|>1/3.                (17)

The endpoint conventions at |t|=1/3 have no surface effect. Set
beta=19/36. Equations (2) become

    nu_-=nu_+=(18/19)eta_z,
    nu_0=(18/19)eta_0
          +(9/19)1_{|t|<1/3}dt  on each edge.       (18)

Here is one exact physical normal-preserving martingale. Send the
(18/19) baseline at every base identically. On each middle edge, send
the remaining source (9/19)dt, |t|<=1/3, in equal thirds to

    (0,n+3t e),   (-1,n+3t e),   (1,n-3t e).       (19)

Its source base and tangent barycenters are zero and t, respectively;
its normal coordinate is unchanged. Each branch of (19), after the
change of variable t -> +/-3t, has target density 1/19 on the full edge.
Together with the baseline, this gives target eta at every base.
Thus (3) holds for this actual cap law, with exactly the normalization
beta in (18), not merely for invented source densities.

At a middle source in the central third, each endpoint conditional is
a point mass at the corresponding location in (19). The endpoint
conditional pairing is therefore FORCED. Its midpoint is n. Consequently
on every edge

    gamma_- = gamma_+ = (1/19)dt,
    tau({n})=2/19,
    rho restricted to this normal = (2/19)delta_(n,0,n),
    D({n})=2 beta (2/19)=1/9.                      (20)

The endpoint flows have constant bounded densities with respect to
actual face length, whereas rho has an atom at the relative interior
of each middle edge. Thus rho is not even absolutely continuous with
respect to eta_0. No finite estimate rho<=C eta_0 follows from (1)-(3),
the common endpoint target surface bounds, or exact tight contact.
No choice of conditional pairing for THIS martingale removes these
atoms. In fact these same data admit a different entire martingale with
a diffuse midpoint law. On each edge first transport nu_0 to
(21/19)dt: keep density min{dnu_0/dt,21/19} fixed and send the excess
6/19 on [-1/3,1/3] equally to t-2/3 and t+2/3. Each outside interval
receives its missing density 3/19, and the two displacements have mean
zero. Given this intermediate tangent point, choose target base zero
with probability 19/21 and each endpoint with probability 1/21.
Keep the original endpoint sources fixed. The complete target is again
eta. The two conditional endpoint tangent laws now agree; their
diagonal pairing gives rho=(1/19)eta_0. Thus the obstruction is to an
automatic bound for a given physical martingale. It does not refute an
existence theorem selecting a better entire martingale.

The example does not assert an ordinary critical cap law or a joint
body minimum. Indeed every cap in (16) has volume 20/3 out of total 12,
fraction 5/9, different from beta=19/36. This distinction is essential:
the example refutes a density consequence of the stated actual
cap-law/martingale geometry, not every strengthening using a critical
volume budget. It is not an OC counterexample.

## 5. Planar selection: a dominated midpoint law after rebuilding the transport

In d=2, for polygonal fibers, there EXISTS a replacement of Pi with
the same source nu, the same target eta, and the same physical endpoint
crossflow measures gamma_-,gamma_+, such that the midpoint law obeys

    rho_max <= eta_0.                               (21)

It remains one normal-preserving physical martingale, and one conditional
endpoint pairing gives (14)-(15) simultaneously for every ambient cap.
The old conditional middle-source kernels are allowed to change. This
distinction is indispensable, as Section 4 demonstrates.

Fix a normal n with crossflow mass m=tau({n})>0. Both endpoint support
faces are edges. Choose a unit tangent e. Their crossflow measures,
in tangent coordinates, are gamma_-,gamma_+, each of mass m and each
bounded above by one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Let Q_-,Q_+ be their
increasing mass-coordinate quantiles on (0,m). The comonotone pairing
is the pushforward of dr by (Q_-(r),Q_+(r)). Its midpoint law is the
pushforward by

    Q(r)=[Q_-(r)+Q_+(r)]/2.                         (22)

It lives on the actual middle edge: (8) gives the tight support height
and (1) gives actual midpoint inclusion.

Here are the two facts needed for the construction, with their proofs.

**Maximality in convex order.** Let xi be ANY coupling of the endpoint
measures and let rho_xi be its midpoint law. For a real threshold k,
restrict xi to the event (x_-+x_+)/2>k, whose mass is r. Each resulting
coordinate marginal is a submeasure of its endpoint measure of mass r.
Its coordinate integral is at most the upper-r quantile integral. Thus

    int (x-k)_+ d rho_xi
      <= [int_(m-r)^m (Q_-+Q_+)/2 dt] - k r
      <= sup_(0<=s<=m) int_(m-s)^m [Q(t)-k]dt
       = int_0^m [Q(t)-k]_+dt.                     (23)

The last equality uses only that Q is increasing. The upper-tail bound
for a submeasure follows by comparing its density, between zero and
one, with the top-r threshold selector; at a threshold atom any unused
fraction can be filled there. The endpoint measures here are nonatomic,
but that elementary bound also holds with atoms. Both midpoint laws
have the same mass and first moment. Every continuous convex function
on their fixed compact interval is an affine function plus an integral
of these call functions against its nonnegative distributional second
derivative (or a uniform limit of convex polygonal functions). Hence

    rho_xi <=_cx rho_max.                           (24)

**Density bound.** If a measure has density at most one, its quantile
obeys Q_i(t)-Q_i(s)>=t-s for 0<s<t<m; otherwise an interval of that
shorter length would carry the larger mass t-s. Generalized quantiles
and one-sided limits give the same assertion at jumps. Consequently

    Q(t)-Q(s)>=t-s.

The inverse image under Q of an interval of length l has length at most
l. This proves rho_max<=Lebesgue measure on the actual middle edge,
without assuming smooth or positive endpoint densities. More generally,
if the two densities are bounded by positive constants c_-,c_+, the
same proof gives the sharp bound

    d rho_max/dx <= 2/(1/c_-+1/c_+).                (25)

Uniform measures on intervals of lengths m/c_- and m/c_+ give equality
in (25). Empty crossflow needs no construction.

For the ORIGINAL conditional pairing in Section 3, combine (14) and
(24) at this one normal:

    nu_(0,n) <=_cx eta_(0,n)+2rho_old,n
              <=_cx eta_(0,n)+2rho_max,n.          (26)

All measures have the same finite mass. There is therefore a compact
one-dimensional martingale from nu_(0,n) to the last measure. This
standard convex-order existence assertion is exactly the equal-mass
case of Section 1 of
`candidate 6eda5637cc09a539`:
finite source/target feasibility follows from a max-of-affines Farkas
separator; source-cell means and barycentric target-grid expansion
preserve convex order; compact weak limits preserve the barycenter.
Equal masses force its target submeasure to be the whole target.
Thus no martingale attainment or smoothness premise is added in (26).

Split each intermediate target using the Radon--Nikodym decomposition
of eta_(0,n)+2rho_max,n. For the eta_0 part retain base zero. For the
2rho_max part disintegrate the comonotone endpoint pairing over its
midpoint and choose its two endpoints with probabilities one half.
Their full physical average is that midpoint, including its normal
height because h_-+h_+=2h_0. Composition therefore preserves the original
source's continuous and base barycenters. The resulting targets are
exactly eta_(0,n), gamma_(minus,n), gamma_(plus,n).

Keep every endpoint-source row of the old Pi. Their target marginals
are the original residuals eta_+-gamma_+ and eta_--gamma_-, so the new
full target is eta. Repeating at the finitely many crossflow normals
constructs the claimed Pi. At zero-crossflow normals the old rows can
be retained. The tuple law for its endpoint branches is built in this
composition, so the simultaneous cap inequality is retained, not
reoptimized cap by cap.

## 6. Arbitrary planar convex fibers and surviving cap selectors

The selection in Section 5 also extends to arbitrary planar convex
fibers, using the already proved contact-area inequality (10). A planar
body has at most countably many positive-length support edges. Modify
the transport separately at the normals of the middle body's edges
which have positive tau mass. At every such normal both endpoint
crossflow measures have length densities at most one, so Section 5
applies verbatim. A countable union of these Borel kernel modifications
is measurable and preserves the full marginals.

At all remaining normals the middle support face is a single point,
apart from the countable edge normals carrying zero tau. The old rho
is already concentrated at that support point. Its normal marginal
tau is bounded by S_0 by (9)-(10). The normal disintegration of eta_0
at a singleton support face is the point mass at the same point.
Consequently the old rho restricted to these remaining normals is
already bounded by eta_0. Keep the old transport there. Combining both
parts proves (21) for arbitrary planar convex bodies.

No multidimensional convex-order maximality is asserted. The call
argument (23) is a one-dimensional tangent argument; in dimensions
d>=3 the contact faces have dimension at least two and this proof does
not supply an analogous dominating midpoint coupling.

For the selected planar law, (15) remains literal closed-cap credit.
In addition, rho_max<=eta_0 removes artificial mass on the endpoints
of a proper middle chord. Since gamma_+<=eta_+ and gamma_-<=eta_-,
all proper endpoint traces also have
zero boundary-plane mass. Thus for a cap proper on all three fibers
its actual trace selectors agree with the corresponding literal bits
on these measures, and (15) is an inequality for those selected traces.
The same is true for full or empty statuses separated from support.
Positive-length supporting coincidences still require their actual
allocations; this theorem does not choose or replace those allocations.

## 7. Exact scope of the midpoint improvement

The aggregate planar theorem forgot the base labels. Equations (7)-(9)
recover its nonaffine-weight error as actual balanced endpoint crossflow
and make strict midpoint support surplus kill that error. Equations
(12)-(15) additionally retain one physical midpoint law and simultaneous
literal cap credit. These statements are stronger data than a numerical
surface-area bound alone.

The missing conversion is explicit. Convex order in (14) is insufficient
for source-cap domination. A given conditional law may be singular, but
in the plane Sections 5-6 show that rebuilding the entire middle
transport repairs this while preserving the old endpoint target flows.
Arbitrary supporting allocations still need their own coupled selector
implication. Nothing here packs these local identities into a parity-two
budget or supplies a classwise Gamma bound.
